THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 18.12.2023, ALONG WITH Crl.MC.8235/2022,
THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 CRL.MC Nos.8221/2022 & 8235 OF 2022  3  ORDER
These petitions have been filed by the accused in Crime Nos.3026/2021 and 3027/2021 of Kothamangalam Police Station, Ernakulam District.

Crime No.3026/2021 was registered alleging commission of offences under Sections 376(2)
(n), 376(3), 363, 370 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4(2) r/w 3(a), 6 r/w 5(1) of POCSO Act.

Crime No. 3027/2021 was registered alleging commission of offences under Section 376(2)
(n) of Indian Penal Code.
The petitioner/accused is common in both the cases.
He is alleged to have entered into sexual relationship with the victim at a time when she was a minor and also after she attained the age of majority on the false promise of marriage.
In regard to the offences committed at a time before the victim attained the age of majority, Crime No.3026/2021 was registered.
In relation to offences committed after the victim attained the age of majority, Crime No.3027/2021 was registered.

The proceedings arising out of Crime No. 3026/2021 is now pending as S.C.
No.167/2022 on the file of the Additional CRL.MC Nos.8221/2022 & 8235 OF 2022 District &
Sessions Court (POCSO), Muvattupuzha and proceedings arising from Crime No.3027/2021 are pending as S.C. No.390/2022 before the Additional District and Sessions Court (For the Trial of Cases Relating to Atrocities and Sexual Violence Against Women and Children), Ernakulam.
2.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the aforesaid crimes came to be registered on the basis of some misunderstanding.

It is submitted that after the aforesaid crimes Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122589147/
2 were registered, a marriage was solemnized between the petitioner and the defacto complainant/victim.

entities.text: crimes Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He refers to the documents produced as Annexure-2 in both these petitions to contend that the marriage between the petitioner and the defcto complainant/victim took place on 6.7.2022.

It is submitted that the petitioner and the defacto complainant/victim are now residing as husband and wife and therefore, the proceedings against the petitioner may be quashed taking into consideration the above situation and in the light of the law laid down by this Court in Vishnu V.
State of Kerala (2023 (4) KHC 1).
CRL.MC Nos.8221/2022 & 8235 OF 2022 3.

entities.text:
Vishnu V.
State of Kerala (2023 (4) KHC 1)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Public Prosecutor would confirm that the petitioner and the defacto complainant/victim/2nd respondent in both cases are living together as husband and wife.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent , I am of the view that, the proceedings against the petitioner can be quashed in the light of the law laid down by this Court in Vishnu (supra).

In Vishnu (supra) this Court held that where the continuance of the proceedings might be prejudicial to the victim and would not be the best interest of the victim, the proceedings can be quashed in exercise of the jurisdiction vested to this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

In the facts of the present case, the allegations on the basis of which Crime No.
3027/2021 was registered relates to a period after the victim attained the age of majority, while the allegations which lead to registration of Crime No.3026/2021 relates to a period before the victim attained the age of majority.

A perusal of Annexure-2 marriage certificate will show that the petitioner and the victim/2nd CRL.MC Nos.8221/2022 & 8235 OF 2022 respondent have solemnized a marriage and it is stated that they are now living together as husband and wife.

Taking the aforesaid facts into consideration and being a respectful agreement with a view taken by this Court in Vishnu (supra), I am of the view that the proceedings can be quashed in exercise of the jurisdiction vested to this Court under Section 482 CRPC.
Accordingly, Crl.M.Cs are allowed.

The proceedings in S.C. No.167/2022 on the file of the Additional District & Sessions Court (POCSO),
Muvattupuzha arising out of Crime No. 3026/2021 of Kothamangalam Police Station and S.C.
No.390/2022 on the file of the Additional District & Sessions Court (For the Trial of Cases relating to Atrocities and Sexual Violence Against Women and Children), Ernakulam arising out of Crime No.3027/2021 of Kothamangalam Police Station, Ernakulam shall stand quashed as against the petitioner.
